findings.finding: The re-read-failure arm returns exit 1, but step 3 documents exit 1 as 'the submit failed and the change is not merged'. When the submit times out and the re-read also fails, the merge state is unknown (Gerrit may well have merged — the incident class). Exit 1 then asserts 'not merged', which the script cannot know. findings.suggested_fix: Either add a distinct exit code (e.g. 3 = INDETERMINATE: submit outcome unknown, check change status before retrying) or redefine exit 1 in the docstring as 'not merged OR merge state unknown'. Add a disposition line per arm: hashtag → warn/continue; 409 → exit 2; merged → 0; not merged → 1 (safe to retry); re-read failed → indeterminate (not safe to blindly retry).

findings.finding: The success test for the error-then-MERGED path is 'status is MERGED and the requested revision is one of the change's revisions'. Any old patchset of the change is 'one of the change's revisions', so the script exits 0 and prints 'merged (revision <sha>)' even when a different, newer patchset was what merged. That contradicts the purpose of a revision-pinned 'safe' submit. The check needs to tie the merged revision to the requested one. Gerrit's rebase-on-submit creates a new patchset, so the link is that the merged patchset is the submit-time rebase of the requested revision, not mere membership in the revision list.

findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 2, specify the re-read as `_request(base, 'GET', f'/a/changes/{change}?o=ALL_REVISIONS', auth)` and test membership with `args.revision in (detail.get('revisions') or {})`. Add a Testing bullet: the submit raises 502, the re-read returns status MERGED, current_revision=<rebased sha> and revisions={<requested sha>:…, <rebased sha>:…}, and the result is exit 0.
